key_insight: The paper introduces “frame width” as a new code parameter and shows how to design group-valued quantum codes with full regular low-weight logical bases, revealing a tradeoff between distance and the ability to realize complete low-weight canonical logical operators.
engineering_relevance: This helps estimate logical gate and decoding overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computing by identifying when low-weight logical operator sets can be systematically constructed and certified.
method: Define frame width f as the minimum weight cutoff that allows a complete canonical logical basis.
Derive structural results for group-valued CSS codes, including obstructions for odd-order groups and a sufficient full-rank condition for power-of-two groups.
Demonstrate the framework on lifted-product and pair-partition code families, plus a symmetry-reduced, stabilizer-pruned exhaustive distance certification method.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit constructions and certifications, including an [[1088,128,22]] LP code with f=22 and an [[1024,256,24]] PP code with f≤27, as well as exact distance proofs for LP examples with over a thousand qubits.
watch_item: The low-weight basis property is not universal: some code families face fundamental obstructions, and achieving the proved frame-width optimum can depend sensitively on the group structure and code construction.
paper_title: Designing Group-Valued Codes with Full Regular Low-Weight Bases
